setup: Two particles, zero-g. A: 0.010 kg sphere moving +X at 40 m/s. B: 100 kg box, 0.5 m side, at rest, DYNAMIC. No routes loaded. One contact episode. Variant B-held: B is turtle-anchored or EXTERNAL.
question: With NO effects in play, what must the engine produce, and what is the largest thing an effect may add on top of it?
expected: Free B: the pair leaves with one common velocity. Momentum is conserved: p = 0.400 kg*m/s before and after. The impulse is the reduced mass times the approach speed, (0.01*100)/100.01 = 0.0099990 kg times 40 = 0.39996 kg*m/s. B gains 0.004 m/s, A ends within 0.004 m/s of B. Kinetic energy falls from 8.000 J to 8.0e-4 J: 99.99 percent of the bullet's energy is dissipated, and that IS the physics of an inelastic strike, not a loss of fidelity. Held B: A stops dead, B is unmoved, and the 0.400 kg*m/s A could not deliver is booked as refused momentum. Neither variant requires an effect. The correct answer to the simplest experiment is produced by physics alone.
composition: The identity case, and the measurement every other experiment is taken against: a run with an empty route table must be bit-identical to a run with no router compiled in. Naive handling: the current effect spelling knockback:<speed> accepts an author-declared absolute magnitude, so a route may write knockback:50 on this contact and deliver 100 kg times 50 m/s = 5000 kg*m/s out of an event that carried 0.4. That is energy creation by authoring, and no amount of review prevents it while the slot accepts an absolute magnitude.

[E] refused ledger, physics_system_v4.cpp:607-624 and include/logosphere/physics/physics_system.h:401-423, booked at three linear sites (:2857 warm start, :3431 normal, :3600 friction). [GAP] PhysicsConfig::restitution is declared at include/logosphere/physics/physics_system.h:53 and has ZERO readers in src (grep over src and include: one hit, the declaration). Every free-pair contact in v4 is perfectly inelastic, so a bounce cannot come from a material property today. [GAP] no general continuous collision detection: swept_aabb_vs_aabb exists (src/core/narrow_phase.cpp:19) but its only callers are FK and locomotion (src/core/particle_dynamics_system.cpp:8, src/animation/humanoid_locomotion.cpp:6079). 40 m/s is chosen so the striker stays inside a 0.5 m box within one substep; a real bullet speed tunnels.

notes: bounce is a material outcome, not a route outcome, and the material parameter that would produce it has no reader. Any route naming bounce today names something the engine cannot do.

setup: One 1 kg sphere falling into one large mud particle whose InteractionProfile declares drag_coefficient 100 kg/s and buoyancy_factor 0.4, and whose category/mask decline rigid contact with the sphere. Gravity 9.81 m/s^2 along -Z.
question: What is an interaction when the other party is not a surface? There is no contact point, no normal, and no episode of touching, only a volume the body is inside.
expected: The sphere relaxes toward the medium's own velocity with time constant m/c = 0.01 s and settles at terminal velocity where drag balances gravity net of buoyancy: v = m*g*(1-B)/c = 1*9.81*0.6/100 = 0.0589 m/s downward. Energy falls monotonically and every joule is booked to the drag bucket. There is no normal, so nothing in the answer may reference one; the result is identical on a wall, on a ceiling and in zero-g because the term it uses is the gravity VECTOR, not an up axis. The sphere never bounces: a medium has no elastic term.
composition: Two KINDS of thing act on one body: a continuous field (per frame, force-shaped, no normal) and, when it reaches the rock at the bottom, a rigid contact (episodic, impulse-shaped, with a normal). They do not compete because they are different pairs. The precedent that matters: rigid contact and medium are ALREADY mutually exclusive for a pair by construction, since should_contact routes a pair to one or the other and a filtered pair never reaches the narrow phase. Naive handling: model mud as a contact with high friction. Then a normal must be invented for a body with no surface, and the only inventions available are the world-up axis (INV-6 violation) or the centre-to-centre direction, which points at the mud particle's centre rather than out of the mud.
carrier: [E] apply_volume_forces, src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp:644-698: linear drag toward the medium's own velocity, buoyancy against the gravity vector, directional field, applied once per frame with substep dedup, and the intruder is kept awake so it cannot freeze mid-medium. [E] medium enter/exit episodes and their VolumeEvents, :180-200. [E] the mutual-exclusion contract, include/logosphere/interaction/particle_interaction_system.h:11-19. [E] drag dissipation bucket, src/core/physics_system_v4.cpp:215 and LEDGER 2026-08-15 (C7). [GAP] there is no MEDIUM_SUSTAIN occurrence: the force pass runs every frame, but only enter and exit are events.
forces: A kind of effect that no contact vocabulary covers: MEDIUM/FIELD, continuous and force-shaped. Fields compose by vector addition, which is associative and commutative, so they need no arbitration at all. It also sets the pattern for exclusion: make excluded kinds unrepresentable for a pair rather than checked at runtime.
notes: The engine's drag is linear (Stokes-shaped), not quadratic, and integrates once per frame rather than per substep. Real mud is a Bingham plastic with a yield stress that holds a body still until a threshold shear. Nothing in the profile expresses a yield stress, so 'the sphere sinks slowly' is expressible and 'the mud holds the sphere' is not.

setup: GEDANKEN-1's bullet. The wall is now TWO 50 kg boxes joined by one weld (nail) gluon with breaking_force 700 N. The bullet strikes the first box square.
question: One occurrence, two consequences: an impulse exchange and a change in the structure. Who decides the break, and out of whose budget is it paid?
expected: Under the engine's tear law the weld does NOT break, and no impact can make it break. Welds break on FORCE = impulse/dt sustained at or above the threshold for 12 CONSECUTIVE frames. The bullet delivers 0.4 kg*m/s in one frame: 0.4/(1/60) = 24 N against 700 N, and even a strike thirty times larger clears the threshold for one frame out of the twelve required. The ledger recorded the general form on 2026-08-15: an impulse cannot break a nail, a WEIGHT can. So the physically correct answer today is that the wall holds, and the game-desirable answer (a bullet shatters a plank) is not reachable through the tear law at all.
composition: If a route may name the break, a game rule decides a structural physical outcome and the energy question becomes acute: the separation work plus the fragments' kinetic energy must come out of the striker's 8 J, not out of nothing. Naive handling: a shatter effect that removes the bond AND deposits a full knockback on both fragments; the fragments leave with energy nobody paid for and the bullet keeps its own. Correct handling needs the WRAP operator: capture the occurrence's measured momentum once, split it into declared shares summing to at most one, spend each share on exactly one consequence.
carrier: [E] weld tear law, force_over_frames >= 12, src/core/physics_system_v4.cpp:4396-4419. [E] fibre tear by strain (the one tear law for force-bounded bonds), :4424-4440. [E] mark_gluon_for_removal, :4417. [GAP] no impulse or energy criterion for breakage anywhere; no fracture effect; no fragment generation.
forces: The WRAP operator, and the rule that ONE occurrence carries ONE budget from which every momentum-carrying and every energy-consuming consequence is apportioned. Raises the fork: is breakage-by-impact a missing physics law or an authorable effect?
notes: The 12-frame rule is not a defect on its own terms; it exists because impulse-derived force is dominated by the damper under sustained rub and tore every grass bond. But it means the engine currently has no mechanism by which a fast, light body breaks anything, which is a large hole for any game with projectiles.

setup: Two particles, no humanoid. D: 70 kg, motion authority EXTERNAL (a writer owns its position), driven along +Y at 1.5 m/s. T: 200 kg trunk particle, DYNAMIC, held by gluons anchored to the turtle. D walks into T.
question: What must happen when a volitional body meets a rooted one, and who pays for the stop?
expected: D stops. T deflects within its anchor's elastic range and returns. Nobody gains energy. The magnitude is checkable: were both free, the impulse would be the reduced mass times the approach, (70*200/270)*1.5 = 77.8 kg*m/s, giving T 0.389 m/s. WHAT THE ENGINE DOES TODAY: D is EXTERNAL, so inv_mass_momentum(D) returns 0 and the row's effective mass is T's alone. Cancelling a 1.5 m/s approach then costs 200*1.5 = 300 kg*m/s, all of it loaded onto T, which leaves at 1.5 m/s. That is 3.9x the honest impulse, concentrated into one frame instead of the tenth of a second a real stop takes. The trunk being kicked is the mechanism that tore canopies off trees earlier in the campaign.
composition: The correct outcome is UNREACHABLE from the effect layer, because the defect is in the PRICE of the row, not in what is done with the result. No effect may repair it: an effect pushing the trunk back would be a second corrector on a pair that already has one (INV-22) and unbooked momentum (INV-7). The repair is the one INV-31 already made for the sleep cache, applied to the other cache: price the EXTERNAL body at its TRUE mass, let the solver compute the interaction honestly, refuse and book the half the writer will not take, and let the writer decide what to do with it. physics_system_v4.cpp:515-526 states that argument for sleepers in so many words; KINEMATIC is the remaining pre-solve guess.
carrier: [E] EXTERNAL priced as infinite mass, src/core/physics_system_v4.cpp:532-537, and the row build reading it at :1381-1382. [E] refusal booked at three linear sites (:2857, :3431, :3600); angular refusals are booked nowhere (LEDGER 2026-08-14). [E] take_refused_impulse drain, :613-624. [E] impulse inbox with no default consumer, src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp:265-283. [GAP] no drain is wired to any writer.
forces: The AUTHORITY-CHANGING kind, and the encode/decode boundary in its purest form: physics hands the writer a measured quantity (the booked impulse) and the writer spends it inside its own model. Also a candidate law: an authority cache must be PRICED like the sleep cache, not guessed before the solve.
notes: This is the scene the owner named when boarding the router. The finding here is that the router is the right consumer of the answer and cannot be the answer.

setup: Two particles. D: 70 kg, EXTERNAL, at rest, held by a named writer. B: 10 kg boulder, DYNAMIC, striking D along +X at (a) 1.0 m/s and (b) 8.0 m/s.
question: When does the writer keep authority and absorb the strike, and when does it hand the body to the solver?
expected: Priced honestly (GEDANKEN-4), the reduced mass is 8.75 kg, so the strike would impart 0.125 m/s at 1 m/s and 1.00 m/s at 8 m/s. Both outcomes, absorb and release, are legitimate physics; which one a game wants is policy. The discriminator MUST be the imparted velocity and never the impulse: 70 kg*m/s means nothing until it is divided by the mass it acts on. INV-10 says this verbatim, that a raw impulse threshold is a shrug to a branch and a shove to a leaf.
composition: absorb and release are two answers to ONE question, who owns this body's motion next frame. INV-7 says that question has exactly one answer; INV-22 says one mechanism owns a pair. So this pair of effects cannot accumulate, cannot be usefully ordered, and must not last-writer-win: they are SINGLE-ASSIGNMENT. Two routes both matching with authority effects is a conflict to report, not a race to run. Naive handling: run both, and the strike is delivered twice, once by the solver taking the released body and once by the writer spending the booked impulse.
carrier: [E] the authority state, src/particle_types.h:78-89, whose header already says KINEMATIC is a transient authority and not a label. [E] a working total release path (unregister_humanoid) and a working per-entity recursive walk, src/kg/entity_physical_state.cpp:34-78, armed at src/core/engine.cpp:445-453 and with zero callers in worldgen, animation or examples. [GAP] no partial release, no named holder, no leak sweep; INV-32 is a candidate only, docs/todo_plans/MOTION_AUTHORITY_DESIGN.md:356.
forces: The SINGLE-ASSIGNMENT property and its home: any kind whose effects answer a question that has exactly one answer. This is the algebra's first hard conflict class, and it is distinct from a tie in the claim order.
notes: Where the threshold comes from is unresolved and this study does not invent one. What a derivation would have to be a function of is stateable: the body's mass, the support polygon its writer stands on, the height of the centre of mass above that polygon, and the corrective authority the writer has left. None of the four is exported today.

setup: Three parties. W: a body already carrying state burning, set thirty frames earlier by MEDIUM_ENTER into a fire volume and still inside it. Bl: a bullet with property material=silver, striking W at 12 m/s. F: the fire, a medium profile.
question: Two things are happening to one body at the same instant. What is the interaction called, and what is the total consequence?
expected: There are TWO occurrences, not two routes on one occurrence: MEDIUM_SUSTAIN(W,F) and CONTACT_OPEN(W,Bl). They are different pairs, so they do not compete for meaning. The body is on fire AND is being shot, and both are true. What they can compete for is anything the body has only one of: its motion authority, and any single property both want to write. Damage is not one of those; it is a numeric accumulator, and 5 J/s of burning plus 3 J of silver simply add.
composition: The ordering hazard is exact and worth writing down. Give the fire route the effect state.set:material=charred, and give a third contact route the condition self material=charred. Under sequential semantics the answer depends on which occurrence was drained from its queue first, which is an accident of engine plumbing. Under SNAPSHOT semantics, where every condition in a frame is evaluated against the state as it stood when the frame's occurrences were harvested and all writes commit afterwards, the third route does not match this frame and does match the next one, whatever the harvest order was. Snapshot makes matching a pure function of the frame's start state, hence order-independent, hence deterministic without anyone having to reason about it. The cost is honest and stated: a chain advances one link per frame.
carrier: [E] two independent occurrence sources exist today: contact episodes, src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp:291-376, and volume episodes, :180-200. [E] the latent nondeterminism the snapshot rule also fixes: rules_ is an unordered_map and every matching rule fires in unspecified order, :364-369, member at include/logosphere/interaction/particle_interaction_system.h:335.
forces: The split the router asserted and this experiment derives: MEANING is elected, one name per side per occurrence; CONSEQUENCES accumulate wherever their deltas are disjoint or additive. And snapshot-evaluated conditions as the mechanism that makes MERGE commutative rather than merely usually-commutative.
notes: The owner's phrase 'silver bullet AND the werewolf is on fire' turns out not to be a contest at all. Reading it as one occurrence with two claims is the mistake; it is two occurrences on two pairs, and the only real contest is over the body's single-valued resources.

setup: The owner's chain, minimally: one EXTERNAL hand particle owned by an animation writer, one fire medium particle, one 40 kg cabinet particle.
question: Where does each link live, what crosses the physics/animation boundary in each direction, and what may an effect NOT do at each crossing?
expected: L0 the hand enters the fire: PHYSICS/geometry, MEDIUM_ENTER. L1 the hand is burning: STATE, a KG property write, and a bus event for free. L2 the entity panics and retracts: GAME DECISION, made by a behaviour system reading the state change. The router does not produce it and no effect may perform it. L3 the hand flies: ANIMATION, a drive; the writer owns the position and physics sees the animated result. L4 the hand hits the cabinet: PHYSICS, CONTACT_OPEN. L5 the cabinet does not absorb the momentum: PHYSICS, MOMENTUM_REFUSED, booked. L6 the hand bounces: EITHER the writer releases authority and physics produces the trajectory, OR the writer spends the booked impulse inside its own clip. It is never the router computing a path. L7 the contact ends: PHYSICS, CONTACT_CLOSE. Exactly two quantities cross the boundary and they cross in opposite directions: physics hands the writer an occurrence carrying a measured momentum and a geometry; the writer hands physics a position claim and an authority state. Nothing else passes.
composition: The chain is a fixed point of the frame rule. Links 3-4, 4-5 and 6-7 each require a physics step regardless of the effect language, so the snapshot rule from GEDANKEN-6 costs the chain nothing it was not already paying. Naive handling, and the shape that must be unwritable: one route firing on MEDIUM_ENTER that emits the whole sequence including where the hand ends up. That route is an animation written as data; it fabricates every trajectory in the chain and is indistinguishable from correct behaviour until something else in the scene moves.

[E] L3 the post-physics writers, src/core/engine.cpp:1267-1268. [E] L4 CollisionEvent to RigidContact, include/logosphere/physics/physics_system.h:66-91 and src/core/engine.cpp:1237-1248. [E] L5 the refused ledger. [GAP] L6 has no release mechanism (INV-32 aspirational) and no drain wired. [GAP] L7 CONTACT_CLOSE is not produced: open_contacts_ is overwritten without a diff at particle_interaction_system.cpp:374, while the volume path does the diff at :188-200.
forces: Termination. An effect's writes are visible to the NEXT frame's snapshot and never to this frame's matching, so no chain can close a loop inside one frame and per-frame work is bounded by occurrences times candidates. Cross-frame cycles remain possible and are the author's, not the engine's.
notes: Five of eight links are carried by mechanisms in the tree. The two missing engine pieces are the same two the router names: the close occurrence, and the release path.

setup: GEDANKEN-1's contact, carrying 0.400 kg*m/s. The struck side matches two routes, each carrying knockback:0.6: one CLAIM route from the body's own table and one OBSERVE route added by a combat system.
question: What bounds the total momentum an interaction may deliver?
expected: 0.48 kg*m/s would be delivered against 0.400 carried: 120 percent of the momentum and, on a 1 kg body, 144 percent of the energy. The bound is not a policy choice. An interaction can deliver at most what it carried; a contact is a passive element that does no positive work (INV-17), and energy is never created (INV-3).
composition: Two ways to hold the bound, and they are not equivalent. (a) A SHARED BUDGET: effects draw from the occurrence's momentum until it is exhausted and an overdraw is refused loudly. (b) SINGLE-ASSIGNMENT: at most one momentum-carrying effect runs per occurrence per side, a second is a conflict. (b) is preferred, and the reason is structural rather than aesthetic: under (a) the outcome depends on the order in which effects drew, so the language must define a draw order and every author must reason about it; under (b) there is nothing to order. It also lands where GEDANKEN-5 arrived independently, which is the argument for making it a property of a KIND rather than a special case.
carrier: [E] deposit_impulse accumulates within a frame so opposing deposits cancel rather than race, src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp:265-283. [E] nothing drains the inbox by default; an unclaimed impulse is a game that has not wired its mover, src/interaction/contact_response.cpp:154-156. [GAP] the deposited magnitude has no relation to the occurrence's momentum: knockback takes an absolute speed, contact_response.cpp:157-166.
forces: The taxonomy's central split: kinds that touch a conserved quantity are SINGLE-ASSIGNMENT, kinds that do not ACCUMULATE. Together with GEDANKEN-5 this is the second instance of the same conflict class, which is what makes it a kind property rather than a rule about knockback.
notes: Note which side is bounded. The bound is on what may be DELIVERED to a body, not on how many routes may match; observers that only emit events are unbounded and harmless. EFFECT_ALGEBRA_DESIGN.md section 4.3 sharpens option (b) further: if single-assignment kinds are legal only on CLAIM routes, and exactly one CLAIM route is elected per (occurrence, side), this table refuses to LOAD and no runtime check is needed at all.

setup: GEDANKEN-1's bullet and wall. The bullet's own route names its side pass_through. The wall's own route names its side blocked. One contact.
question: Two systems name the same event differently. Is that a contradiction to be arbitrated?
expected: No. The two names are statements about two different bodies, and the engine already evaluates a contact once per side with the normal re-oriented so that each side reasons about itself. 'I was blocked' and 'I passed through' are descriptions of experience; the single physical outcome was decided by the solver before either was named. So an interaction has ONE physical outcome and up to TWO meanings, one per side. There are two elections, not one, and they never touch.
composition: What this rules out is the reading in which pass_through is an ACTION. A route cannot make a body pass through another: whether a pair produces rigid contact at all is a declared pair policy on the interaction profiles, consulted by the broad phase long before the router exists. A route naming pass_through on a pair that did contact is describing something that did not happen. The self/other asymmetry that already governs effects, where conditions ask about other and effects act on self, is what keeps the two elections separate, and it is also why an entity with no rule of its own is unaffected by everything.
carrier: [E] per-side evaluation with the normal flipped, src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp:238-262 and :356-370. [E] the asymmetry contract, include/logosphere/interaction/contact_response.h:38-66. [E] the pair policy that decides rigid contact, include/logosphere/interaction/particle_interaction_system.h:11-19.
forces: The unit of election is (occurrence, side), not occurrence. And the line between NAMING and CAUSING: an outcome name is a description; only an effect acts, and only on self.
notes: The router design frames simultaneous claims as one contest. Per-side evaluation means there are two, each with one winner, which removes a whole category of imagined conflict.

setup: One 45 kg box at rest on the turtle, settled, contact sustained indefinitely. One route: on CONTACT_SUSTAIN, outcome rest, do damage.apply:1.0.
question: What does an effect mean when the occurrence never ends?
expected: Sixty damage per second for lying still. The physics says the opposite: a resting contact does zero work, and a settled scene performs zero corrective work (INV-24, whose origin is 1955 corrective firings of 290 nm each on a scene at rest). The absurdity is not in the number, it is in the UNIT: 1.0 of damage per frame is a quantity whose meaning changes with the timestep, which is the defect INV-10 names, one dimension over. A per-frame effect must carry a rate and be scaled by dt; a per-episode effect must be attached to an occurrence that has episodes.
composition: Effects therefore have a CARDINALITY as well as a kind: once-per-episode, per-frame-rate, or idempotent-state. The composition rule is a TYPE rule, not a runtime check: an effect registered once-per-episode cannot be attached to a SUSTAIN occurrence, and a per-frame effect must declare a unit with a time in the denominator. The engine already has the machinery to express this, since schema/physics.yaml carries a value, a UCUM unit, a group and a doc string for every physics constant under INV-29.
carrier: [E] episode throttling means ON_CONTACT fires once per episode today, src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp:309-312, so this class of error is currently UNREACHABLE, and becomes reachable the moment CONTACT_SUSTAIN exists (router slice S1). [E] effect arguments are unit-free strings parsed by each effect, src/interaction/contact_response.cpp:17-26. [E] the units precedent, schema/physics.yaml constants_registry, 68 constants with UCUM units.
forces: Units and cardinality declared at effect registration and checked at load. This is the mechanism that makes INV-10's spirit, and its timestep sibling, enforceable rather than reviewable.
notes: The cheapest experiment in the set and the one that most directly changes the language: it is the reason effect registration must carry a type, not just a function pointer.

setup: One contact between a bullet and a werewolf. Two rules match. Rule G states no condition and its effect writes status=struck. Rule S states the condition with_type:Werewolf and its effect writes status=seared. Both are ON_CONTACT. Both apply, because every matching rule applies.
question: Both writes land on the same property of the same body in the same frame. Which one does the world keep?
expected: seared. A rule that describes fewer situations is the one its author wrote FOR this situation; a rule with no condition is the fallback for everything else. So the specific rule's write must land last, which means the general rule must apply FIRST. This is the cascade every author already knows from CSS, and it is the only ordering under which a physical default can be stated once and overridden exactly where it matters. The reverse order makes the blanket rule win every argument and makes specificity pointless.
effects_required: state.set (a STATE effect, last-write-wins per property)
composition: Order is only OBSERVABLE where two effects write the same target. That is the entire reason ordering exists and it also bounds how much ordering the engine must get right: not every pair of rules, only pairs whose effects collide. See GEDANKEN-12, which is the same setup with the collision removed. The implementation today orders on ONE BIT, whether the condition string is empty, which is correct for this case and silent about every finer one (type depth, threshold tightness, unlike conditions).
carrier: [E] every matching rule applies, the ON_CONTACT loop in src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp. [E] the order is computed once at load, the sort in load_rules_from_kg, tier = condition.empty(). [E] measured in both authoring directions, tests/test_rule_order_determinism.cpp.
forces: General applies first so the specific write survives. Ordering matters only where writes collide.
notes: Written AFTER the code it describes, which inverts the discipline the owner set: the thought experiment is supposed to come first and the implementation is supposed to answer it. Recorded this way deliberately rather than backdated.

setup: GEDANKEN-11 exactly, with one change: rule G writes status=struck and rule S writes temperature=800. Two rules, one contact, two different properties.
question: Does the order in which they apply matter?
expected: No. The two writes commute; any order leaves the same world. Ordering is unobservable here, and an engine that agonises over it is solving a problem it does not have.
composition: This halves the problem and points at a missing capability. The engine does not need a total order over all rules. It needs one over rules whose effects COLLIDE, and every other pair may run in any order with identical results. A load-time pass could compute the colliding sets and report exactly those, which turns 'is my rule table ambiguous' from a question nobody can answer into a diagnostic printed at startup. It cannot do that today: an effect is an opaque string resolved through a registry at apply time, so the engine has no idea what any effect WRITES. Effects declare what they DO, not what they TOUCH.
carrier: [E] effects are opaque expressions dispatched by name, ContactEffectRegistry::apply in src/interaction/contact_response.cpp. [GAP] nothing anywhere declares an effect's write set, so collision detection is not expressible.
forces: An effect must declare its write target, not only its behaviour, or the engine can never tell a real ambiguity from a harmless one.
notes: The cheapest useful version is a declared target string per registered effect, checked only at load.

setup: A 2 kg stone falls onto a wooden floor and lands at 3 m/s. The route table is empty, or holds only routes that do not match. Physics resolves the contact normally.
question: What does the engine say happened?
expected: Today: nothing. The contact is resolved and no name is produced, so a world with no authored rules is a world where nothing is ever described. The owner's ruling is that the engine emits the PHYSICS RESPONSE instead: a name taken from what was measured (impact, at 3 m/s, stone against wood), carrying no game meaning at all. We cannot enumerate every interaction a rich world contains, but we can approximate the ordinary ones from physics and let authored rules replace them where it matters.
effects_required: none: the default names, it does not act
composition: The default is not a row in the table. It is what the table's ABSENCE means, which is why GEDANKEN-11's ordering has to put general before specific: the physics default is the most general statement there is, and every authored rule is a refinement of it. It must also cost nothing when nobody listens, and it must never be able to suppress physics. A route may rename what happened; it may not un-happen it. Every fall-through is counted by (occurrence kind, self type, other type) so that authoring effort can follow measured frequency instead of imagination: the thought experiments we can invent are the defaults we preload, and the counter finds the ones we failed to invent.
carrier: [E] GEDANKEN-1 requires an empty table to be bit-identical in MOTION to no router at all, which the default must not disturb. [GAP] no fall-through path and no counter exist.
forces: The default's vocabulary is bounded by what the engine can measure. bounce needs restitution, which is declared with zero readers; roll needs angular state at the contact; topple is unimplemented. The default may only say what physics can prove.
notes: Boarded as D6. The counter is independent of everything else and can run before the rest exists, which is the point of building it first.

setup: One contact. Rule A applies first and its effect writes a property on the struck body in the knowledge graph. Rule B applies second and its condition reads that same property. Both were authored independently, by different systems, neither aware of the other.
question: Does B see A's write, inside the same contact?
expected: It must not. GEDANKEN-6 settled that matching is evaluated against the world as it stood when the frame's occurrences were harvested, so that no answer depends on plumbing order. If B can see A's write then adding a rule silently changes which OTHER rules match, and the table stops being readable by a human: you can no longer tell what a rule does by reading it, only by knowing everything that runs before it.
effects_required: a STATE effect that writes the graph
any condition that reads the graph
composition: The engine is HALF there, which is worse than either end. The per-side view snapshots both entity types before the rule loop runs, so with_type is genuinely order-independent. The same view also carries a live pointer to the graph, and with_part_type dereferences it at evaluation time. No shipped effect writes the graph (knockback deposits an impulse, emit_event emits), so this does not bite today. It bites the day a game registers a state-writing effect, which is a thing the registry exists to allow. The fix is not to remove the pointer, since conditions legitimately need to read the graph. It is to make those reads go through a frame snapshot, or to defer every write to the end of the frame.
carrier: [E] the view stores a live graph pointer, view_from in src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp. [E] the two entity types ARE copied into the view before the loop, same function. [E] with_part_type follows ctx.kg at evaluation time, src/interaction/contact_response.cpp.
forces: Snapshot semantics is a property of the whole system, not of one condition. Half a snapshot is a trap, because it works until it does not.
notes: Found while auditing what the ordering change actually guaranteed. Nothing triggers it today, which is exactly why it should be closed before something does.

setup: The ontology declares SilverBullet is_a Bullet. The striker is a SilverBullet whose material property reads silver. Two rules match, describing the same object two ways: rule A addresses the TYPE (a silver bullet), rule B addresses the SUPERTYPE plus a property filter (a bullet whose material is silver). Neither states anything else.
question: When one rule names a type and another names that type's ancestor plus a filter the type implies, which is more specific?
expected: Neither, derivably. The two rules do not cover the same objects, because a property is mutable at runtime: a SilverBullet whose material was changed to charred is matched by A and not by B, and an ordinary Bullet plated silver mid-play is matched by B and not by A. The match sets CROSS. Neither contains the other, so no ordering between them is a fact, and any total order imposed on them is a convention.
effects_required: any two effects that collide, per GEDANKEN-11
composition: Both plausible placements silently pick. Ranking property-filter count first (today) resolves the pair without ever consulting the ontology. Ranking subsumption depth first resolves it without ever reading the instance. The owner's ruling refuses a single global answer and makes the policy a property of the HIERARCHY, declared in the schema: SPECIALISE where a subtype is meant to override its parent, ENCAPSULATE where the type is a closed box and a filter on the parent has no business reaching inside. That does not dissolve the crossing; it converts an underivable fact into a declared input, which is INV-29's shape applied to routing.
carrier: [E] the lattice machinery exists, OntologyRegistry::isSubtypeOf and ancestorsOf in include/logosphere/kg/ontology_registry.h. [E] property mutation is in the vocabulary, the state.set effect and GEDANKEN-6's charred material. [GAP] facets do NOT inherit, explicitly and by decision, EntityTypeDef in the same header, so this reasoning covers types only.
forces: Two descriptions of one thing are not one description. Where sets cross, the order must be declared by whoever owns the hierarchy, not inferred by the engine.
notes: R5 on the board. Residual owed: the default policy for a hierarchy that declares neither, and whether the annotation sits on the root type or on every type.

setup: A human's hand touches a cabinet. One rule addresses the creature: with_type:Human. Another addresses the body part: with_part_type:Hand. Both match this contact.
question: Is a rule about the hand more specific than a rule about the creature it belongs to?
expected: Not derivably, and for the same reason as GEDANKEN-15. The hand rule matches every hand in the world, including a hippo's. The creature rule matches every part of that human, including its foot. Neither set contains the other; they cross at exactly one point, which is this contact.
composition: This is the argument for hierarchical ADDRESSES, and it is a structural argument rather than an expressiveness one. Human/**/Hand names the intersection of the two crossing sets, and the intersection IS a subset of both, so a third rule written that way is unambiguously more specific than either. Without addresses the engine holds two incomparable rules and has no honest way to order them; with addresses the ambiguity is not resolved, it is made impossible to express by accident, because the author who means the intersection can now say so. That is the difference between a syntax that is convenient and one that earns its place.
carrier: [E] with_type compares the other party's type exactly, src/interaction/contact_response.cpp. [E] with_part_type resolves the part through the graph, same file. [GAP] no address syntax exists anywhere; conditions are flat name:args strings.
forces: Hierarchical addressing earns its place by making incomparable rules comparable, not by being richer.
notes: The cleanest first-principles justification for the address design in INTERACTION_ROUTER_DESIGN.md.

setup: A world is running. A combat system decides that from this moment silver burns werewolves, and creates the route as a knowledge-graph entity while the simulation continues. A werewolf is already in contact with a silver blade; that contact episode opened three frames ago.
question: When does the new route take effect, and what happens to the episode already open?
expected: The route should take effect at a frame boundary, never mid-frame, and an episode already open should finish under the table it started with. An interaction whose meaning changes halfway through is an interaction with two meanings, which GEDANKEN-9 already ruled out per side.
composition: Three gaps, all mechanical. First, a route written to the graph does nothing at all until someone calls the loader again; there is no signal and no watch, so 'the combat system adds a rule' is not a supported action, it is a convention. Second, rules can be added and overwritten by id but never individually removed: the only removal clears everything, so a route is permanent for the life of the process, and a temporary buff cannot be expressed. Third, reloading rebuilds the whole order, so a route added mid-episode changes the outcome of contacts already in flight.
carrier: [E] rules enter only through load_rules_from_kg, which assigns by id and never clears, src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp. [E] the only removal is clear(), which drops profiles, rules, armed entries and open episodes together, include/logosphere/interaction/particle_interaction_system.h. [E] the order is rebuilt on every load call.
forces: A table that changes while the world runs is part of the world's input, and its edit points must be as well defined as a frame boundary. Insertion without removal is not a routing table, it is an accumulator.
notes: This is the seam the owner asked for, 'allow the routing to be modified by any other system, like combat'. It does not exist yet.

setup: A knowledge-graph-backed creature touches a procedurally generated pebble that was never entered into the graph. Physics resolves the contact exactly as it would for any pair.
question: What can a route say about the pebble?
expected: Nothing, and the engine must SAY that rather than fall silent. Physics happens regardless of graph membership; meaning does not. A contact with a party outside the ontology is unnameable, and that is a fact worth reporting rather than a case worth skipping.
composition: Today the outcome is correct and silent, which is the problem. The side whose own party is unresolved is skipped outright. The creature's side is still evaluated, with the pebble as the other party, and any condition naming the other party's type fails closed because the type string is empty. So an author who writes with_type:Pebble gets no match, no effect, and no diagnostic, and cannot distinguish 'the pebble is not that type' from 'the pebble is not in the graph at all'. Those are different problems with different fixes and they look identical. The same counter GEDANKEN-13 asks for answers this too: count contacts that were unnameable because a party was outside the ontology, and the class becomes visible instead of invisible.
carrier: [E] a side whose own party is unresolved is skipped, the ON_CONTACT loop in src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp. [E] the view leaves the other type empty when the entity is invalid, view_from in the same file. [E] with_type compares against that empty string and fails, src/interaction/contact_response.cpp.
forces: Silence and 'no match' look identical. Fail closed is right; failing closed without a count is how a whole class of contact stays invisible.
notes: Pairs with GEDANKEN-13: one counter serves both, keyed by occurrence kind and the two type strings, with the empty string meaning 'outside the ontology'.

setup: A 1 kg cube spawns at rest on the turtle with rotation_x/y/z all zero and rotation_q identity. Nothing ever applies a torque. It sits for 600 frames. This is the case that describes almost every body in a world: floor tiles, walls, rocks, spawned scenery.
question: Under a change that makes the quaternion the only orientation truth, what must this body do differently?
expected: Nothing whatsoever, bit for bit. This is the migration's safety property and the baseline every other orientation experiment is measured against: for a body that never rotates, quaternion truth and Euler truth are the same state, and a run under the new representation must be bit-identical to a run under the old one. If it is not, the defect is in the publish path and not in anything about rotation.
composition: The same role GEDANKEN-1 plays for the router. Establish the identity case before touching anything, so that every later difference has exactly one candidate explanation. It also prices the change honestly: the owner ruling is that Euler becomes a published VIEW for every body, so every body pays a quaternion-to-Euler conversion each frame it is awake. For the overwhelming majority of bodies that conversion converts identity to zero, which is the argument for skipping it on the sleep path rather than for keeping the flag.
carrier: [E] the publish exists today for quat-driven bodies only, integrate_angular_velocities in src/core/physics_system_v4.cpp. [E] Quat::to_euler_zyx, src/math/quat.h:298-311.
forces: Establish the no-op case first. Every later difference then has one candidate cause.
notes: Cheapest possible first test of the campaign and the one that should be written before any code changes.

setup: A body is given yaw = +pi/2 as an Euler triple, which by the engine's documented convention means facing +X (east). It is converted to a quaternion, integrated for one frame with zero angular velocity, and published back to an Euler triple.
question: Does it still face east, exactly?
expected: It must, to the last bit that matters downstream. The engine's whole orientation convention is stated in Euler terms in CLAUDE.md: rotation_z is clockwise viewed from +Z, yaw 0 faces +Y, yaw +pi/2 faces +X. Vision, AI direction estimation and motion planning all assume it. A round trip that is off by a sign or a convention does not fail loudly; it makes every downstream subsystem slightly wrong in ways that only appear under rotation and look like rendering artifacts.
composition: The conversions are already built as an inverse pair and both handle the handedness explicitly: from_euler NEGATES Z because the input is clockwise while axis-angle is counter-clockwise, and to_euler_zyx emits -atan2 for the same reason. So the round trip is intended to be identity away from the gimbal boundary, and the header says so. What has never been measured is whether it IS, for bodies that never carried a quaternion before, across the full range of the three angles rather than at a few sample poses. Under the ruling, every such body starts carrying one.
carrier: [E] from_euler negates Z for the CW convention, src/math/quat.h:319-322. [E] to_euler_zyx emits -atan2 for the same reason, :305. [E] the convention itself, CLAUDE.md orientation section. [GAP] no test sweeps the round trip.
forces: A convention that lives in one representation must survive the trip through the other, or every consumer of direction is quietly wrong.
notes: A sweep over the three angles is a twenty-line test and should exist before the representation changes, not after.

setup: A body is pitched until sin(pitch_y) exceeds 0.9999, roughly 89.2 degrees, and then yawed. A falling plank tumbling end over end passes through this pose twice per revolution.
question: What does the published Euler triple say, and does anything downstream believe it?
expected: The quaternion holds the pose exactly. The published Euler triple cannot: at that boundary the conversion FORCES out_x to zero and folds the body's roll into the yaw term. Two genuinely different orientations publish as the same triple. This is not a defect in the conversion, it is what Euler angles are; it is the reason the quaternion should be the truth.
composition: The important question is not whether the publish is lossy there, since it provably is. It is whether anything downstream INTEGRATES from the published value rather than merely displaying it. A renderer reading a lossy triple draws one frame slightly wrong and recovers. A system that reads the triple, computes from it and writes back has just destroyed the body's real orientation, and the loss is permanent. Under Euler truth that is what tumbling through vertical does today. Under quaternion truth the internal state survives and only the view is degraded, which is the whole argument in one case.
carrier: [E] the gimbal branch forces out_x = 0 and folds roll into yaw, src/math/quat.h:306-310. [E] the header states the round trip is stable only for |sin(pitch_y)| <= 0.9999, :292-296.
forces: A lossy VIEW is acceptable. A lossy TRUTH is not. The distinction is which one anything writes back to.
notes: The concrete scene is a plank tumbling end over end, which the Rube Goldberg machine can stage.

setup: One humanoid arm particle in one frame. Three systems have an opinion about its orientation: the FK cascade writes an Euler triple from the animation clip, the yaw cascade writes rotation_z directly from the cascaded body yaw, and a quaternion joint drive integrates rotation_q in the solver.
question: Who owns this particle's orientation, and how does the engine know?
expected: Exactly one owner, and the engine should know from ONE mechanism. Today it knows from three, none of which is aware of the others.
composition: Enumerated, because three is not a figure of speech here. First, `is_quat_driven`, a per-particle boolean deciding whether rotation_q or the Euler triple is the truth. Second, a `drive_set` inside the yaw cascade, which returns early with the comment 'physics owns rotation_z on this particle' and is a hand-maintained set rebuilt by the animation layer. Third, `solver_mode`, which decides whether the solver may move the body at all. Three overlapping answers to one question, exactly the shape the STATIC eradication and the KINEMATIC ruling were about, one layer down and in the angular half where nobody had looked. Making the quaternion the single truth removes the first. It does not remove the second, and the second is the one that will still be there afterwards.
carrier: [E] the flag, src/particle_core.h:77-86. [E] the drive_set early return, apply_yaw_cascade_rotations in src/animation/humanoid_locomotion.cpp:3527ff. [E] solver_mode, src/particle_types.h:78-89.
forces: One question, one mechanism. Three mechanisms means at least two are silent most of the time and disagree occasionally.
notes: The drive_set is the residual the ruling does not reach, and it should be boarded separately rather than assumed to fall out.

setup: A quat-driven body, mid-frame, after the solver has integrated rotation_q but before the Euler publish has run. Two subsystems ask for its orientation in the same instant: the narrow phase, to build its oriented collision box, and the inertia projection, to price an angular constraint row.
question: Do they get the same orientation?
expected: No, and this is verified rather than argued. The narrow phase reads rotation_q when the body is quat-driven and builds from Euler otherwise. GetInertiaAboutAxis builds its body frame from rotation_x, rotation_y and rotation_z UNCONDITIONALLY, with no knowledge of the flag or the quaternion. So for exactly the class of body the flag was invented for, the shape the solver collides is oriented by the quaternion and the inertia it is priced with is oriented by a triple that has not been refreshed yet.
composition: This is a live disagreement in the tree today, not a hazard the migration would introduce, and it is the strongest single argument for the ruling. It is also INV-20's shape: a constraint row priced with one orientation and applied to geometry built from another is a row priced for a different world than the one it acts on. Under quaternion truth with an unconditional publish the two sources converge by construction and the class of defect cannot be written.
carrier: [E] the narrow phase picks rotation_q when quat-driven, src/core/narrow_phase.cpp:677-678. [E] GetInertiaAboutAxis builds its body frame from the Euler triple only, src/particle_core.h:302-309. [GAP] nothing measures the divergence.
forces: Two subsystems reading one body's orientation from two fields is a disagreement waiting for a pose that separates them.
notes: Measure the angle between the two orientations across a tumbling body before changing anything; that number is the campaign's before-value.

setup: A perfectly spherical 0.2 kg pebble rolling down a slope. It is rotating genuinely and continuously, and its orientation is unobservable to its own collision geometry, because a sphere is the same shape from every angle.
question: Does this body need an orientation published every frame?
expected: Its collision geometry never asks. Its rolling behaviour does, through the contact-point velocity v_com + omega x r, but that reads angular VELOCITY rather than orientation. Rendering asks only if the surface carries a texture or a mark. So the honest answer is that a sphere needs omega, not a published orientation, and the publish is pure cost for it.
composition: This is the cost half of the ruling and it deserves a number rather than a shrug. The study named the cost of quaternion truth plainly: every body pays the publish. The question is which bodies can skip it without reintroducing a per-body representation flag, which is the thing being removed. Two candidate answers that are NOT a flag: skip the publish for sleeping bodies, since a body at rest has an orientation that is not changing and INV-24 says a settled scene does no work; and derive the need from SHAPE, since a sphere's orientation is unobservable to geometry by definition rather than by declaration. The second is attractive and needs care, because it is only true while nothing reads a sphere's orientation, and a textured sphere breaks it.
carrier: [E] the rolling definition depends on omega and the contact radius, not on orientation, EFFECT_ALGEBRA_DESIGN.md interaction floor. [GAP] the publish has no skip path today because it runs only for quat-driven bodies.
forces: Cost that is uniform is easier to reason about than cost that is conditional. Any skip must derive from physics or from shape, never from a per-body flag, or the flag comes back wearing a new name.
notes: The trap to avoid: 'skip the publish when nothing reads it' is a flag with extra steps.

setup: A 0.5 kg iron cube spinning at 4 rad/s in interplanetary vacuum. No contacts, no bonds, no fluid, nothing within a thousand kilometres.
question: How long does it keep spinning?
expected: Forever, minus nothing. Angular momentum is conserved in the absence of an external torque; that is not a modelling preference, it is the definition of an isolated body. Measured against the engine as it stands: omega is multiplied by 0.95 every substep, four substeps a frame, so the cube retains 0.95^240 of its spin after one second, which is about 4.5e-6. It stops in a second, in vacuum, because a constant said so.
composition: This is DAMPING_FACTOR's disease in the angular half, and the file already says so in its own words. ANGULAR_DRAG's comment reads 'Same INV-19 exposure as DAMPING_FACTOR: absolute-motion damping whose dissipation story is thin. Extracted as-is by decree; any retuning is ledger follow-up.' The extraction campaign made the constant legible, named, unit-tagged and homed, and it WROTE DOWN THE OBJECTION. Nobody came back for the follow-up. INV-29 was satisfied and INV-19 was not, and satisfying the wrong one is how it survived. The linear twin has since been eradicated and has zero readers left; its angular sibling is still applied at three sites.
carrier: [E] ANGULAR_DRAG = 0.95 with the confessing comment, src/generated/physics_constants.h:296-301. [E] applied to omega_z, omega_x, omega_y, src/core/physics_system_v4.cpp:5064, :5086-5087. [E] DAMPING_FACTOR has zero readers left, the eradicated linear twin.
forces: Extraction makes a constant legible. It does not make it legitimate. The two invariants ask different questions and only one of them was asked.
notes: A second angular damper hides in the animation layer as a bare literal, humanoid_locomotion.cpp:5277, const float ANGULAR_DRAG = 0.98f, shadowing the name with a different value and never extracted at all.

setup: A pebble resting on open ground under an open sky. No water volume, no mud volume, no declared medium anywhere near it.
question: What medium is this pebble in?
expected: Air, and the engine's answer IS air, which I got wrong twice before checking. Every moving body already receives quadratic drag against sea-level air density, every substep, in integrate_positions. So the default of every scene is not vacuum, it is one atmosphere, hardcoded. The gap is not that ambient air is missing. It is that ambient air is NOT DECLARABLE: a scene cannot turn it off, cannot change its density, and therefore cannot be set in space, underwater, or on Mars.
composition: Two drag laws now run in the same engine and neither knows about the other. The ambient one is QUADRATIC (0.5 * rho * Cd * A / m), applied per substep inside position integration, and booked to the dissipation ledger. The medium one is LINEAR Stokes, applied once per frame from a declared volume overlap, and booked nowhere. A body inside a declared water volume therefore receives BOTH at once: it is in water and in air simultaneously. That is the real defect, and it is worse than the missing-ambient story it replaces, because it is silent. The ambient law is also motion-blind: cross_section is width*height regardless of which way the body is travelling, so a plank presents the same area edge-on as face-on.
carrier: [E] quadratic ambient drag on every moving body, src/core/physics_system_v4.cpp:4674-4683. [E] RHO_AIR = 1.225 kg/m3 and DRAG_CD = 1.5, src/generated/physics_constants.h:236,240. [E] the second, linear medium drag, apply_volume_forces in src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp:714-716. [GAP] neither law is declarable per scene or per world; a scene cannot be placed in vacuum.
forces: A medium is currently something you enter, never something you are already in. Void is the unstated default of every scene.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-16. The first version of this record asserted 'zero hits repo-wide, the unstated default of every scene is vacuum'. False. The grep searched for ambient, world_medium and the quoted string "air"; the mechanism is spelled RHO_AIR. A filter encodes a hypothesis, which is the failure the global diagnosis rule exists to prevent, committed by the person who quotes it.

setup: A flat wooden paddle, fully submerged inside a declared water medium, spinning about its long axis at 3 rad/s. Alongside it, an identical paddle spinning at 3 rad/s in open air outside any medium volume.
question: Which one slows down first?
expected: The submerged one, by a wide margin: water is roughly 800 times denser than air and the paddle presents a large area to the flow. The engine's answer is that they slow at exactly the same rate, because the only angular dissipation in the tree is a global constant that knows nothing about either body's surroundings.
composition: The medium model applies drag, buoyancy and field forces to LINEAR velocity only. apply_volume_forces writes vx, vy and vz and never touches omega or torque. So a body in water is slowed but never stopped from spinning, and the water contributes nothing to its rotation at all. This is the angular half of GEDANKEN-26's hole, and the two must be fixed together: an ambient medium without angular coupling still leaves ANGULAR_DRAG as the only thing damping a spin, and angular coupling without an ambient medium leaves every body in the open with no fluid to couple to.
carrier: [E] apply_volume_forces touches only vx/vy/vz across drag, buoyancy and field, src/interaction/particle_interaction_system.cpp:714-731. [GAP] no angular term anywhere in the medium path.
forces: Two holes, one constant papering over both. Fixing either alone leaves the constant standing.
notes: The honest replacement for ANGULAR_DRAG is rotational drag derived from the body's extents and the medium's density acting on relative angular velocity, which needs both halves in place first.

setup: The ramp of test_ramp_race, one cube and one sphere released together, run once per surface: ice, stone, tarmac, sand. Only the material changes.
question: Who reaches the bottom first, and what does the answer say about the engine?
expected: It depends entirely on the surface, and that is the point. A sliding body accelerates at g(sin_t - mu*cos_t); a sphere rolling without slipping accelerates at (5/7)*g*sin_t, independent of mu, because rolling dissipates nothing at the contact. On a 40 degree slope g*sin = 6.31 m/s2 and a sphere needs mu >= (2/7)tan_t = 0.240 to roll at all. ICE (mu 0.05): the sphere cannot get the traction to roll, so BOTH slide, both at 5.93 m/s2, and they ARRIVE TOGETHER. That is the only surface where a tie is correct. STONE (mu 0.50): sphere rolls at 4.50, cube slides at 2.55, sphere wins by a wide margin. TARMAC (mu 0.80): sphere still rolls at 4.50, cube crawls at 0.30. SAND (mu 1.10): mu exceeds tan(40)=0.839 so the cube does not move at all, while the sphere still rolls, because rolling needs only 0.240.
composition: The owner spotted this by watching: 'sphere and cube arrive at the same time, which is a no no unless it was ice surface'. The engine is giving the ICE answer on stone, and the reason is D2 1.2: contacts carry no lever arm, so the sphere never spins up and slides like a ball of ice whatever it is made of. Measured in this scene, cube 6.356 m and sphere 6.251 m in the same 4 s, which is a tie inside the noise of two different shapes sliding. This makes the material matrix a DISCRIMINATOR rather than a nicety: the four surfaces give four different orderings, and only one of them is a tie. A test that runs all four cannot be passed by an engine that ignores either rotation or friction.
carrier: [E] measured tie in tests/test_ramp_race.cpp, cube 6.356 m vs sphere 6.251 m with peak |omega| 0.0000 for both. [E] D2 1.2, contact rows carry no lever arm. [GAP] no test anywhere varies the surface material and compares orderings.
forces: A tie between a rolling shape and a sliding one is a statement about the SURFACE. Getting it on stone means the engine is not modelling rolling at all.
notes: Owner directive 2026-08-19: be comprehensive with these tests, ice vs sand vs tarmac. The matrix is cheap: one scene, one material parameter, four runs, four predicted orderings each with closed-form arithmetic to check against.

setup: One 0.4 m stone cube, tilted 20 degrees about Y, dropped from 0.3 m above the floor. Nothing else in the world. The control is the same drop untilted, which must settle flat without inventing any rotation.
question: What orientation does it settle in?
expected: Flat on its face, rotation_y = 0. A rigid cube cannot rest on an edge: the contact acts at the edge, gravity acts at the centre of mass, and at 20 degrees the centre is horizontally offset from the support line, so there is a net torque about the contact edge until a face is down. 20 < 45 degrees, so the nearest face is the original bottom: it tips BACK flat rather than over. Settled state: |rotation_y| < 0.05 rad, centre at z = 0.2, and it must have ROTATED to get there (peak |omega_y| well above zero during settling).
composition: This is the irreducible contact-torque experiment: one body, one floor, one angle, no tangential motion to argue about. It discriminates lock 1 and lock 2 (contact rows carry no lever arm; the torque gate excludes Euler-truth bodies) from everything else, because no friction model and no material property enters the prediction, only geometry. The control drop pins the other direction: an engine that passes by inventing rotation on the FLAT drop has a different bug, so the pair together is the discriminator.
carrier: [E] turtle rows hardcode the Jacobian to (0,0,1) with no contact point, physics_system_v4.cpp:783-791 per ROTATION_CAMPAIGN_DESIGN.md 1.2. [E] the torque apply is gated on is_quat_driven && owner==PHYSICS, :3468. [E] the Euler publish is gated on is_quat_driven, :5110, so even granted torque the rotation would be invisible for an Euler-truth body. [GAP] no test drops a tilted body and asserts its settled orientation.
forces: A cube balanced on its edge forever is a statement that contacts cannot torque. The expected value needs no constant: 20 degrees, nearest face, done.
notes: Owner method 2026-08-19: divide and conquer, G's first, asserts from the G's, measure, then solutions. Prediction for today's engine: it rests tilted at exactly 20 degrees, balanced on an edge, centre high, omega zero throughout.

setup: The same cube, flat, spun about Z at 3 rad/s, dropped from 0.3 m. Flight time sqrt(2h/g) = 0.247 s, about 15 frames.
question: Where is the spin allowed to die?
expected: Only at the contact. In flight there is no torque, so the spin arrives at the floor intact: retention at touchdown > 0.95 up to integrator noise. After touchdown, face friction brakes it: uniform pressure over a square face of side a gives a mean lever of 0.3826a = 0.153 m, so braking torque = mu*m*g*0.153 and, with I = m*a^2/6 = 0.0267m, angular deceleration ~28 rad/s^2 at mu 0.5. Three rad/s dies in roughly 0.11 s, THROUGH friction, with the rotational energy booked to the friction bucket.
composition: The discriminating assert is the FLIGHT half, not the settled half. Today's engine also ends at zero spin, so 'it stops' proves nothing; ANGULAR_DRAG multiplies omega by 0.95 per substep, so after 15 frames of flight retention is 0.95^60 = 0.046. The spin dies in the AIR, before the floor exists. An engine that passes the flight assert and then brakes on the face is doing physics; one that fails it is applying a constant. This is GEDANKEN-25 with a floor attached, and the floor is what turns 'delete the constant' from a wrong fix into a wrong fix that this experiment would catch: bare deletion makes the settled half red instead, because nothing would ever brake the spin.
carrier: [E] ANGULAR_DRAG = 0.95 per substep, physics_constants.h:301, applied at physics_system_v4.cpp:5064,5086-5087. [E] the friction bucket exists (g_dissipation.friction, :3572,:3630) but is file-static with no accessor, so the booking assert is not writable from a test today. [GAP] recorded rather than faked.
forces: Flight conserves; contact dissipates; the ledger says where. Each half kills a different wrong implementation.

setup: The flight frames of GEDANKEN-36, examined one frame at a time. L_z = I*omega_z, and I is constant for the body, so frame-to-frame retention of omega_z IS retention of angular momentum.
question: May any frame of torque-free flight change the body's angular momentum?
expected: No, by definition: dL/dt equals applied torque, and there is none. Per-frame retention in flight must be 1.0 to integrator noise (assert > 0.99 per frame). At contact, L may change only through the contact impulse's moment, and the rotational energy removed must appear in a dissipation bucket, not vanish (INV-3's angular half).
composition: This is the conservation law stated so it can be asserted per frame rather than end to end, which is what makes it divide-and-conquer: an end-to-end retention number cannot tell a constant leak (every frame, everywhere) from an impact loss (one frame, at the floor). Per-frame measurement separates them in one plot. Today's engine leaks 18.5 percent per frame in flight (0.95^4), which no impact story can explain.
carrier: [E] the leak site, physics_system_v4.cpp:5064,5086-5087. [GAP] no angular term in any dissipation bucket: the Dissipation struct books linear KE only, so even a correct friction brake would currently dissipate rotational energy unbooked.
forces: Conservation is asserted per frame or it cannot name its violator.
notes: The [GAP] is itself a finding: when contact braking lands (D2), the friction bucket needs an angular term or INV-3's ledger goes quietly wrong in the other direction.
